newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S TRYBUNA DAILY SEEKS INVESTORS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S TRYBUNA DAILY SEEKS INVESTORS.

text.p: Poland's left-wing daily Trybuna is in talks with investors who could take a yet undecided stake in the paper, the head of the company publishing Trybuna said.

Stanislaw Cwik, also Trybuna's deputy editor, told Reuters the capital would be used to double the daily's circulation, now at 90,000 copies, ahead of parliamentary elections due after August, improve print quality and introduce colour.
"We are in talks with various investors, both Polish and foreign. It is yet undecided what stake we might offer -- whether above or below 50 percent," Cwik said.
"We have not decide either if the investor should buy existing share or take a new share issue," he said.
Cwik said Trybuna, which employes 60 journalists, made a profit in 1996, but said final results were not yet available.
Trybuna is published by the Ad Novum firm owned in 99 percent by the private Fundacja Blizej Swiata>fund set up by Universal .
